newsitem.title: TURKEY: Iraqi Kurd group says Arbil governor in gun attack.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi Kurd group says Arbil governor in gun attack.

text.p: An Iraqi Kurdish group said in a statement on Monday that gunmen had opened fire on the convoy of the governor of Arbil, northern Iraq's administrative centre.
The Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) said two security force members and five civilians were slightly wounded in the attack.
The incident took place at 8.10 a.m. local time (0510 GMT) on Sunday while Arbil governor and regional minister Franso Hariri was on the way to his office, the statement said.
The KDP did not mention any injury to Hariri and said it was "grateful for the governor's safety."
It said initial evidence indicated the involvement of the rival Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) and its politburo member Kosrat Rassoul in planning the attack.
Turkey's state-run Anatolian news agency reported PUK radio as saying that two of Hariri's bodyguards had been killed in the incident and denying that Rassoul was involved.
The rival KDP and PUK have held several rounds of talks in Ankara aimed at forging a permanent peace in northern Iraq following a U.S.-brokered ceasefire last October.
The KDP joined with Iraqi troops to take control of Arbil from the PUK late last year, prompting retaliatory U.S. missile strikes on Iraqi targets.
The clashes gave Baghdad a foothold in northern Iraq for the first time since the end of the Gulf War in 1991.
